newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Geneva bank eyes $500 mln share of Islamic wealth.
newsitem.headline: Geneva bank eyes $500 mln share of Islamic wealth.

text.p: Leading Geneva private bank Pictet & Cie hopes to capture more than $500 million in new Islamic client assets within a year with a debut joint venture targetting the Moslem, a bank official said.
Kamran Amouzegar, in charge of the bank's Middle Eastern business, also told Swiss news agency ATS the Islamic fund market, managed under Sharia law principles, was "immense."

Pictet's Geneva-based joint asset management firm with Kuwait-based Islamic finance company The International Investor (TII), announced on Monday, is the first of its kind in Geneva's lucrative and fee-paying private banking business.
The 50-50 owned firm, Albait, will offer tailored private banking services to Islamic clients from Gulf states.
Western bankers said Middle Eastern money represented an important part of Geneva's private banking market after Anglo- Saxon, German and other continental European clients.

They said the Middle East, as well as Southeast and Far East Asia, account for the bulk of the new wealth that has found its way this year to Geneva, which already caters for the rich Arabs mainly in real estate and tourism businesses.

Like other Islamic banks and finance institutions popular among the world's more than one billion Moslems, Albait will adhere to the principles of Islamic sharia law that bans interest because it is considered usury.
It will concentrate on equities, excluding makers of beer, alcoholic drinks or other products that violate Islamic rules.
Pictet, with $62 billion in client funds including assets under custody, is one of the biggest private banks in Switzerland's notoriously secretive $1.8 trillion asset management industry.
